method.scanPrimitive: git ls-files -z | xargs -0 grep — 1574 tracked files, 1287 of them .ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx/.mjs/.cjs. Untracked files and node_modules are OUT of scope by construction; `git status --porcelain` was empty, so nothing untracked existed to miss.
controls: HOSTNAME CENSUS positive control: the regex 'https?://[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+' over all tracked files returned 132 distinct hosts including 'api.openai.com' (known present at packages/api/src/internal/providers/lib/providers/openai.ts:10) and 'tailwindcss.com' x307. A blind scan would have printed 0 hosts. Vacuity floor: 132 > 0.

HOSTNAME CENSUS negative-direction control: the https-only regex MISSED the two realtime endpoints (wss://api.openai.com/v1/realtime, wss://api.x.ai/v1/realtime). A second pass on 'wss?://' found them plus 9 unrelated ws URLs, so that pass was also non-vacuous. Both passes are reported; the count below is the union.

ADAPTER COUNT positive control: `ls providers/*.ts` = 22 files; `grep -c 'export const .*Provider: Provider'` matched in exactly 19 of them, and `grep -l 'VoiceProvider = {'` matched exactly 2 (grok-voice, openai-voice). 19 + 2 + index.ts = 22, so the file listing and the two symbol censuses agree and neither is vacuous.

DEAD-ROUTER claim positive control: an unanchored `grep -n 'internal/providers'` over ALL tracked files returned 60+ hits across AGENTS.md, docs/, db tests, schema and gateway-client (so the pattern demonstrably sees the string), and packages/api/src/index.ts appeared in NONE of them. A second control: `grep 'authenticateService'` found 13 hits INSIDE internal/providers and 0 outside. Two independent patterns, same conclusion.

SANITIZER CENSUS positive control: grep for sanitizeMessage|sanitizeError|sanitizeFull|getSafeErrorMessage|formatErrorResponse found 16 files including packages/api/src/routes/v1/chat-completions.ts, a known user-facing surface. Floor: 16 > 0.

SDK-DEP CENSUS positive control: the package.json scan found '@ai-sdk/openai' in packages/api/package.json, which is independently proven present by the static import at packages/api/src/lib/chat-core.ts:9. All 15 tracked package.json files were read (list enumerated, not globbed by name pattern alone).

ENV CENSUS positive control: the process.env regex returned 97 distinct names including GROK_API_KEY, independently confirmed at packages/api/src/internal/providers/lib/providers/grok-voice.ts:52 and packages/api/.env.example:108. A second pass covered dynamic `process.env[expr]` access (5 sites, all OAuth/flags, none provider-inference).
limitations: A call-site census using the pattern `name(` MISSES generic calls. Measured directly: `callProviderAPI(` scored 0 in packages/api/src/lib/memory/embeddings.ts and packages/api/src/routes/v1/audio.ts because both call `callProviderAPI<any>(` / `callProviderAPI<Buffer>(`. Every call-site count below was re-run WITHOUT the paren requirement. Any count in this file that still used `(` is flagged in its own evidence.

A single-pattern importer census misses alternate relative specifiers. Measured: `from '.*lib/retry|from './retry` returned 0 importers for packages/api/src/lib/retry.ts, but `withRetry|retry\.js` returned 3 real importers (browser-session, web-scraper, web-search). Every 'has no importers' claim below was therefore re-run against the SYMBOL name, not the path.

Counts of call sites exclude comments only where stated. The provider-conditional census (`provider === '<name>'`) does not filter comments; its 6 hits were each read in context and all 6 are executable code.

grep is line-based. A provider hostname split across a template-literal newline would not match. No such construction was found, but this is an unmeasured blind spot — the finding is 'not observed', not 'absent'.

Reachability claims are STATIC (import graph + Express mount table). They do not account for a runtime `require`/`eval`. No dynamic module loading by string concatenation was found in packages/api/src.

Provider CREDENTIAL VALUES were not read. The store is asserted from the schema (provider_keys.key is a plaintext `text()` column) and from the deploy workflow's secret list; no live database was queried (Mongo is gone, Postgres not reachable from this box).

The `.do/app.yaml` DigitalOcean spec is present in the repo but the deploy pipeline is `.github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml` (ECS). Whether `.do/app.yaml` still governs a running DO app was NOT verified — that requires the DO dashboard, outside this read-only repo scan. It is reported as a hazard, not as live config.
residual: packages/alia-gateway-admin (61 source files) is an operator UI for the deleted alia-gateway. Its dev proxy rewrites /api/providers -> /internal/providers against https://api.alia.onl, and /internal/providers is NOT mounted. I could not classify whether the deployed static site still exists (DO static_sites entry in .do/app.yaml) — that is an infra question, not a repo question.

packages/alia-console documentation pages (sdks.tsx, examples.tsx, quickstart.tsx) print `import OpenAI from 'openai'` 13+ times. This is the OpenAI-COMPATIBLE client library name, not a claim about Alia's backend provider. Whether that counts as a model-abstraction violation is a product call I am not making.

Whether the 15 thin OpenAI-compatible adapters should be ported to Relay or simply deleted depends on whether Relay reuses the Vercel AI SDK. I classified them 'delete' because their entire content is a base URL plus a default model id, both already duplicated in chat-core.ts — but that is a recommendation, not a measurement.

`external_models` (the ZeroEval leaderboard mirror served publicly at GET /external-models) exposes third-party organisation names. It is deliberate per the schema comment, but I could not determine whether the model-abstraction rule was ever consciously exempted for it.

Timeouts for the embeddings modality: packages/api/src/lib/memory/embeddings.ts passes NO `timeout` and NO `maxAttempts`, so it inherits provider-api.ts's maxAttempts=3 and NO per-attempt timeout at all. Whether the absent timeout is intentional is unknown.
I did not classify the ~60 packages/api/src/db repositories beyond the 6 that touch provider tables. Workstream boundaries may need the rest.

items.name: fallback-engine.ts
items.summary: Walks TIER_MODEL_MAPPINGS in priority order, skips providers whose circuit breaker is open, caps key cycling at MAX_KEYS_PER_PROVIDER=3, treats 'format' and 'content_filter' as non-retryable, and records a fallback_events row per resolution.
items.removalGate: Reachable only through model-resolver. Gate: Relay implements tier-ordered failover AND Alia stops needing per-attempt FallbackAttempt data for its own telemetry.

items.name: provider-api.ts
items.summary: The NON-streaming provider call path (images, embeddings, TTS, transcription, audio-gen). Owns key rotation, per-attempt AbortController, DigitalOcean async-invoke branch and the Google Gemini TTS branch. Default maxAttempts=3, timeout OPTIONAL.
items.removalGate: LIVE. Reached from gateway-client.ts:353 (dynamic) and directly from lib/show/show-pipeline.ts:22. Gate: Relay exposes an equivalent multi-modal non-streaming call with key rotation, and all 8 callProviderAPI call sites are repointed.
items.evidence: packages/api/src/internal/providers/lib/provider-api.ts:32-37 (PROVIDER_BASES, only 4 providers have a base URL), :102-103 (maxAttempts default 3), :112-291 (retry loop), :134 (DO branch), :163 (Gemini TTS branch)

items.name: PROVIDER_BASES covers only 4 of 19 providers
items.summary: The non-streaming path only knows base URLs for openai, groq, openrouter and digitalocean. Any other provider appearing in a v1-image / v1-tts / v1-audio tier mapping throws 'Provider "x" has no configured base URL' at attempt time, which the callers swallow as 'try next'.
items.removalGate: N/A — this is a defect to carry across, not to delete. Relay must either cover all providers or reject the mapping at config time instead of at call time.

items.name: provider-health.ts (circuit breaker)
items.summary: Per (provider, modelId) circuit breaker with closed/open/half-open states, a 10s in-process cache, and a 5-minute background interval that half-opens expired circuits. Rate-limit errors deliberately do NOT open the circuit.
items.removalGate: BLOCKS ON THE LOAD BALANCER: packages/api/src/routes/health.ts:79 and :144 call getAllProviderHealth(), and /health/ready returns 503 'no_healthy_providers' when zero providers are healthy. Land a replacement readiness probe IN PRODUCTION before removing this, or the removal is a rolling outage that reports success.
items.evidence: packages/api/src/internal/providers/lib/provider-health.ts:176-212 (isProviderAvailable), :298-323 (monitor, auto-started outside NODE_ENV=test), :57-58 (10s cache); readiness dependency packages/api/src/routes/health.ts:144-147

items.name: key-manager.ts
items.summary: Selects the best provider key (priority order within free/paid group), enforces per-key rps/rpm/rph/rpd/tps/tpm/tph/tpd windows, demotes failing keys to last priority, sets exponential cooldown (30s * 2^n capped 5min), archives after maxTotalFailures, and marks credit-exhausted keys. 10s key cache.
items.removalGate: Removable once Relay owns provider credentials. NOTE the export markKeyCreditExhausted is called from PRODUCT code (agent/runner.ts:704, services/chat.service.ts:286) via gateway-client, so those two call sites must be repointed or dropped first.

items.name: alia-models.ts (ALIA_MODELS catalogue)
items.summary: The Alia-branded model catalogue (14 tiers) plus TIER_MODEL_MAPPINGS re-exported from the generator, and getAvailableModels() which joins circuit-breaker health with an isLegacy flag read from Postgres.
items.removalGate: STAYS IN ALIA — this is the branding layer that makes model abstraction possible and is the only thing that must NOT leak to Relay's vocabulary. What must move is TIER_MODEL_MAPPINGS (the provider routing table), not ALIA_MODELS.

items.name: generate-model-mappings.ts
items.summary: The provider routing table: for each of 14 Alia tiers, an ordered list of createMapping(provider, providerModelId, priority, qualityScore). This is the single densest concentration of provider model ids in the repo.
items.removalGate: Read by gateway-client's getModelMappingsForTier, which 8 product call sites use (images, TTS, transcription, avatars, canvas, chat-completions, voice, chat.service). Every one must resolve tiers through Relay first. NOTE: a live Postgres table `alia_model_provider_mappings` exists but the runtime reads the CODE table, not the table.

items.name: chat-core.ts getAIModel — the LIVE provider construction site
items.summary: THE real inference chokepoint. items.removalGate: Alia must keep FailoverReason as its own vocabulary (credits, retry, UI messaging all key off it). What moves to Relay is the provider-shape PARSING, not the enum.

items.name: sanitizeMessage / redactUnsafeDetail / getSafeErrorMessage / formatErrorResponse
items.summary: Two rules. redactUnsafeDetail is absolute on every surface: credentials, URLs and hostnames, and the ten upstream error codes failover-error.ts classifies on. sanitizeMessage adds product-surface concealment of the 19 PROVIDER_NAMES and the model families in the live routing table, matched as IDENTIFIERS (a proper noun, or a / . - _ = joined token) so ordinary prose survives. #139 ws20 replaced the previous unanchored replace-with-'Alia' behaviour.
items.removalGate: NEVER REMOVE. Its slug list is BUILT FROM provider-names.ts, so deleting that array silently narrows the sanitizer. Anyone deleting the provider directory must keep PROVIDER_NAMES or inline the list here first. sanitize.test.ts walks the live routing table and goes red when it cannot conceal an upstream identifier.

items.removalGate: Bypasses gateway-client entirely, so a facade-level migration leaves it calling the old runtime. Must be repointed explicitly.

items.name: MODALITY chat + streaming: timeouts, retries, fallback, cancellation
items.summary: Global request timeout 80s (chosen to beat a ~120s gateway limit). Per-provider first-byte abort 20s. AI SDK maxRetries=0 so failover is application-level. Provider retry budget = max(tierMappings.length, 5). Time-budget guard breaks the loop with 10s left. auth/rate_limit are KEY-level (retry same provider, next key); timeout/unknown skip the provider. Cancellation: req.on('close') aborts; a mid-stream timeout sends a graceful finish instead of an error. In-stream synthesis retry uses a fresh 30s AbortController.
items.targetPath: relay:chat (Alia keeps the global timeout + SSE contract)
items.removalGate: Relay must expose per-attempt failover semantics OR accept that Alia's 80s budget now covers a network hop it does not control. The 20s first-byte abort is the number most likely to be wrong after the hop is added.

items.name: MODALITY images: timeouts, retries, fallback, cancellation
items.summary: Global 60s AbortController; walk v1-image mappings in priority order with timeout 30s and maxAttempts 1 each (fail fast, next provider); abort checked at the top of each iteration; exhaustion returns 504 if the global abort fired else 503. THREE independent copies of this loop exist (v1/images.ts, agents-avatar.ts, canvas/execute.ts) with slightly different error mapping.
items.removalGate: All three copies must move together; agents-avatar additionally maps content_filter to a 400, which Relay must preserve as a distinguishable reason.

items.name: MODALITY TTS: timeouts, retries, fallback, cancellation
items.summary: Route-level global 55s abort; per mapping maxAttempts 1 and a MODEL-DEPENDENT timeout — getProviderTimeout returns 120s for fal-ai/* models and 15s otherwise. Voice name translated per provider before the call; the real output container is returned separately. S3 upload has its own 15s race. Cached audio on the message short-circuits the whole path.
items.removalGate: getProviderTimeout's fal-ai/ prefix test lives in gateway-client.ts:316-321 — a provider model-id string inside the facade. Relay must own that timing decision.

items.name: MODALITY audio generation: async job, 3-minute budget
items.summary: POST /v1/audio/generate returns 202 with a jobId immediately, then a background worker runs with GEN_TIMEOUT_MS=180s and a 170s provider timeout, maxAttempts 1, single hardcoded provider+model. Result polled via GET /v1/audio/jobs/:jobId; progress pushed over Socket.IO. Credits are finalised at zero on failure.
items.removalGate: The 202-plus-poll shape exists because generation exceeds a proxy timeout. Relay must either keep the async contract or Alia must keep its own job table.

items.name: MODALITY transcription: timeouts, retries, fallback
items.summary: POST /v1/voice/transcribe: global 55s abort, walks the audio tier with timeout 15s and 1 attempt each, endpoint /v1/audio/transcriptions with multipart audio (gateway-client converts base64 to FormData for the local path). Exhaustion returns 503; global abort returns a TIMEOUT code.
items.removalGate: The base64-to-FormData conversion lives in gateway-client.ts:355-366; Relay's contract must accept audio directly.

items.name: MODALITY realtime voice: connection timeouts, inactivity, billing
items.summary: WebSocket handshakeTimeout 10s plus a 10s connect promise timeout. MAX_SESSIONS_PER_USER=5, per-minute billing tick (60s), user-silence timeout 20s, cohost inactivity 30s, cohost check-in wait 15s, MAX_RECENT_TRANSCRIPTS=5, VOICE_MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS=3. No provider FAILOVER at all: a provider socket error closes the session ('provider_error'). Session duration additionally capped by the plan's voice-minutes entitlement.
items.removalGate: This is the only modality with NO fallback. If Relay adds a hop, the 10s connect budget and the 20s silence timer both need re-derivation, and 'provider_error' must not become 'relay_error' in a user-facing string.

items.name: MODALITY embeddings: NO timeout, NO fallback, silent null
items.summary: The only modality with no timeout and no tier mapping: a single hardcoded provider/model, inheriting provider-api's maxAttempts=3 with NO per-attempt timeout, and returning null on any failure so memory search silently degrades.
items.removalGate: A hop to Relay without a timeout means a hung Relay hangs memory writes for as long as the socket stays open. Add a timeout as part of the move, and preserve 1536 dimensions.
items.evidence: packages/api/src/lib/memory/embeddings.ts:20-32 (no timeout/maxAttempts passed); default at packages/api/src/internal/providers/lib/provider-api.ts:103 (maxAttempts=3, timeout undefined)

items.name: Key-level vs provider-level failure discrimination
items.summary: KEY_LEVEL_REASONS = {auth, rate_limit} -> add the key id to failedKeyIds and retry the SAME provider; everything else -> add the provider to skipProviders. This two-tier retry is invisible from outside and is the behaviour most likely to be silently dropped in a port.
items.removalGate: Relay must distinguish 'this credential is bad' from 'this provider is down', or a single bad key takes a whole provider out of rotation for the request.

items.removalGate: Stays; only the provider TABLES leave.

items.name: LIVEKIT_URL / LIVEKIT_INTERNAL_URL / LIVEKIT_API_KEY / LIVEKIT_API_SECRET
items.summary: Voice transport credentials, synced to SSM /oxy/_shared/. Required for POST /v1/voice/token (503 without them).
items.removalGate: Stays with Alia unless Relay terminates LiveKit.

items.name: ALLOWED_SERVICES / ADMIN_USERNAMES
items.summary: Read ONLY by the dead internal-providers auth middleware. ALLOWED_SERVICES has exactly two occurrences repo-wide (.env.example and that file).
items.removalGate: NONE. Note ADMIN_USERNAMES is separately hardcoded as `username === 'nate'` in tool-pipeline.ts:130, so removing the env var does not remove the admin gate.

items.name: VITE_GATEWAY_API_URL
items.summary: Frontend base URL for the dead admin panel; defaults to http://localhost:4150/internal/gateway.
items.removalGate: Goes with the package.

items.name: MONGODB_URI / CA_CERT (legacy)
items.summary: Still declared required in .env.example and .do/app.yaml, still read by lib/db.ts and by the dead internal/providers/lib/db.ts. index.ts's own comment says Mongo no longer exists.
items.removalGate: Not the provider workstream's call alone — routes/v1/audio.ts and other product code still use Mongoose Message models. Flagged because the provider cleanup will surface it.

items.name: deploy-aws.yml secret allow-list (10 entries, ZERO provider keys)
items.summary: Syncs exactly DATABASE_URL, SERVICE_SECRET, TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY, VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY, VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, LIVEKIT_API_KEY, LIVEKIT_API_SECRET, REDIS_URL. No OpenAI/Anthropic/Google/etc. key appears anywhere in the deploy path — confirming provider credentials live only in provider_keys.
items.removalGate: If Relay needs a shared secret from Alia, it must be ADDED here and to terraform in the same change — a render carries forward every secret it is not told to replace, so a half-added secret fails only at scale-up.

items.name: HAZARD: .do/app.yaml sets GATEWAY_API_URL to the deleted gateway
items.summary: Sets GATEWAY_API_URL=http://gateway:9091 AND SERVICE_SECRET on the alia service — the exact pair that flips gateway-client into HTTP mode against a service that no longer exists. It also declares a `gateway` service built with `bun run build:gateway`, a script that no longer exists in the root package.json.
items.removalGate: Verify no DigitalOcean app still reads this file before deleting (see residual). If one does, every inference call is already failing there. The AWS pipeline (deploy-aws.yml) sets neither variable.
items.evidence: .do/app.yaml:43-46 (SERVICE_SECRET + GATEWAY_API_URL), :77-90 (gateway service, build:gateway); root package.json scripts contain no build:gateway or start:gateway

items.name: HAZARD: packages/api/.env.example documents a provider architecture that no longer exists
items.summary: Header states 'Provider API keys (OpenAI/Anthropic/etc.) are NOT configured here — they live in the alia-gateway service. The API reaches it via GATEWAY_API_URL + SERVICE_SECRET.' The gateway is deleted and keys live in Postgres. It also lists MONGODB_URI as required and never mentions DATABASE_URL.
items.removalGate: A wrong instruction survives forever in a dotenv template. Fix in the same change that touches gateway-client, or the next operator wires GATEWAY_API_URL at a dead host.

items.name: HAZARD: warmupGatewayClient and syncZeroEval never run (Mongo-gated boot)
items.summary: startBackgroundServices() is called only from connectWithRetry()'s success branch. The file's own comment states Mongo no longer exists and the retry loop therefore never succeeds, so the gateway-client cache warm-up and the leaderboard sync are dead in production. warmupProviders() is NOT affected — it sits outside the gate and does run.
items.removalGate: Relevant to the epic because 'we warm the model cache at boot' is false today; any Relay design that assumes a warmed cache is designing against fiction.
items.evidence: packages/api/src/index.ts:338-344 (startBackgroundServices), :386-398 (only caller), :435-446 (the comment), :449 (warmupProviders, outside the gate)

items.name: HAZARD: provider credentials held in process memory for 10 minutes
items.summary: The provider-instance TTLCache is keyed `${provider}|${baseURL}|${apiKey}` with ttlMs 10 minutes and maxSize 200, so up to 200 plaintext provider credentials sit in a module-level map in Alia's process, and each appears in a cache KEY.
items.removalGate: Disappears for free once Relay holds the credentials — this is one of the strongest arguments for the epic, and worth stating in the PR.

items.name: Documentation naming providers and provider files
items.summary: Five documents describe the provider runtime by FILE PATH (alia-models.ts, generate-model-mappings.ts, fallback-engine.ts, provider-names.ts, tts-providers.ts, gateway-client.ts) and by provider name. AGENTS.md additionally states the gateway-client seam rule.
items.removalGate: Per the org standard, docs/comments/log strings are where a wrong statement survives forever. Every file path named in these five documents is a candidate for deletion by this epic; sweep them in the same PR, not after.

items.name: livekit-agent.ts (LiveKit <-> provider audio bridge)
items.summary: Joins a LiveKit room as an agent participant and pumps PCM16 audio both ways between LiveKit tracks and the provider realtime WebSocket, plus transcripts over the data channel. 24 kHz mono.
items.removalGate: STAYS IN ALIA — it is LiveKit plumbing, not provider logic. What changes is WHICH socket it pumps into. Note it imports AgentDataMessage/LiveKitAgentBridgeRef type-only from internal/providers/lib/types-voice.js, so a directory-scoped deletion breaks its typecheck.

items.name: credits-manager reserveVoiceCredits / finalizeVoiceCredits
items.summary: Per-minute voice billing. voice-session-manager reserves 1 minute up front at the mapping's costPerMinute and finalises on close, separately for the primary and the cohost agent.
items.removalGate: STAYS IN ALIA (credits are Alia's), but costPerMinute comes from the ModelMapping, i.e. from the provider routing table. Relay must report a per-minute cost or voice billing silently reserves at zero.

items.name: db/providers/* repositories (4 files)
items.summary: aliaModelRepository, modelConfigRepository, providerKeyRepository, externalModelRepository — every statement against the four provider tables. Consumers: key-manager (providerKey), alia-models (listAliaModels for isLegacy), routes/external-models + sync-zeroeval (external), and the dead admin routes/seeds for the rest.
items.removalGate: SPLIT: externalModelRepository is the leaderboard mirror and stays. The other three go with their tables. aliaModelRepository.listAliaModels is the one live read outside the dead subtree (the isLegacy flag) and needs an Alia-side home.

counts.adaptersDetail: 19 text-chat Provider adapters + 2 realtime VoiceProvider adapters; 22 files in the directory including index.ts. Only the 2 voice adapters are reachable at runtime.
counts.gatewayClientImportersDetail: 21 non-test importer files plus 1 test that vi.mocks the module. Of the 21, 3 are billing-only (plan-access, stripe-prices, billing) and touch no provider data. The larger real chokepoint is chat-core.ts with 32 non-test importers.
counts.providerHostnamesDetail: 19 inference hostnames (openai, openai-realtime-wss, anthropic, google, groq, openrouter, digitalocean, xai incl. wss, mistral, deepseek, cerebras, together, fireworks, perplexity, novita, hyperbolic, sambanova, cohere, replicate, cloudflare — counted as 19 distinct hosts since api.openai.com and api.x.ai each serve both https and wss) plus api.zeroeval.com which is NOT inference. Excludes the unbounded dynamic asset URLs returned by DO async-invoke.
counts.providerEnvVarsDetail: GROK_API_KEY, GATEWAY_API_URL, SERVICE_SECRET, ALLOWED_SERVICES, ADMIN_USERNAMES, DATABASE_URL, LIVEKIT_URL, LIVEKIT_INTERNAL_URL, LIVEKIT_API_KEY, LIVEKIT_API_SECRET, MONGODB_URI, VITE_GATEWAY_API_URL. Exactly ONE (GROK_API_KEY) is a provider credential, and it is inert.
counts.providerSdkDepsDetail: 11 declarations across 5 distinct packages: ai (api, integrations), @ai-sdk/openai (api, integrations), @ai-sdk/anthropic (api, integrations), @ai-sdk/google (api, integrations), openai (alia-codea, alia-codea-cli, alia-cowork). The 3 openai declarations are CLIENTS of Alia's own API, not provider deps. Excludes the 5 LiveKit packages (voice transport).
